conventions.convention: One Newtonian inertial affine chart is fixed; time, position and mass use seconds, metres and kilograms. Under t′=t+β, x′=Rx+vt+a₀, scalars compose with the inverse event map, velocity gains the boost, acceleration rotates, and stress transforms as RσRᵀ.

B is nonempty, bounded and open, its closure lies in an open reference chart O, and I is a nonempty open interval. The motion χ is jointly C², each χ_t is injective with invertible spatial derivative, and J=det D_Xχ is positive on I×B.

The model density is strictly positive and C¹ on an open neighborhood of the full swept closure. Material subregions B′ are nonempty bounded open subsets with closure contained in B. General Lebesgue mass constructions assume countable choice.

Traction t(n) acts on the material opposite the side toward which n points; boundary normals are outward, t=σn, and positive pressure corresponds to σ=−pI. Matrix divergence is initially the row divergence g_i=Σ_j ∂_jσ_ij.

Force and torque balances apply to every admissible finite piecewise-C¹ region, with face integrals and surface-null edges. Both balances use the same volume density ρb−ρa, and no body or surface couples occur.

The elastic branch uses e=(Dξ+Dξᵀ)/2, constant Lamé parameters μ_s>0 and λ+2μ_s/3>0, and W=λ(tr e)²/2+μ_s tr(e²). Its replacements by reference density and reference-coordinate derivatives are declared small-displacement idealizations.

Periodic fluid variables are dimensionless: y=x/L_*, τ=t/T_*, T_*=L_*/U_*, U=u_phys/U_*, Π=P_m/(ρU_*²), and ν_*=η/(ρU_*L_*). The unit torus has normalized measure and pressure has zero mean. Constant-density inviscid Euler is adopted separately from the barotropic branch.

The string has c=√(τ_s/ρ_ℓ), displacement and initial displacement have length units, and initial velocity has speed units. Fixed-end series require odd 2L-periodic C⁵ displacement and C⁴ velocity data; mode indices start at n=1.

load_bearing.statement: A motion χ:I×O→R³ is C²; each χ_t is injective with invertible total derivative; J=det D_Xχ_t>0 on I×B. The spatial velocity satisfies u(t,χ(t,X))=∂_tχ(t,X), and labels follow frame-time-parametrized C² worldlines.

Under countable choice, the stated motion, an open J₀ with closure contained in I, and a C¹ field on a neighborhood of the swept region, F(t)=∫_{χ_t(B)}f(t,x)dx is differentiable with F′=∫_{χ_t(B)}(∂_tf+div(fu))dx; along each label, d[f(t,χ(t,X))]/dt=D_tf(t,χ(t,X)).

Under countable choice, the smooth kinematic model, positive C¹ density and mass balance for every material subregion, ∂_tρ+div(ρu)=0 on the current regions. Conversely, that equation on a neighborhood of the swept region implies mass balance. D_tρ=−ρ div u, ρ(t,χ(t,X))J(t,X) is constant along each label, and ∂_tJ=J div u.

For every admissible region D at every time, ∫_{∂D}t(s,y,ν_D)dS+∫_D(ρb−ρa)dy=0, and for every fixed origin x₀ the corresponding integrals crossed with y−x₀ also sum to zero, with the same volume-force density and no couples.

Under countable choice and the model fields and balances (F),(T), at each time and on each stated bounded open W inside the current region there is a unique continuous stress matrix with t(s,y,n)=σ(s,y)n, t(s,y,−n)=−t(s,y,n), and σ(s,y)ᵀ=σ(s,y).

Under countable choice, the stated mass and momentum balances and regularity, ρD_tu=ρb+g on the current regions, where g_i=Σ_j∂_jσ_ij. With the same kinematics, continuity and a C¹ symmetric stress representing traction, this local equation conversely implies force balance on every admissible region and integral momentum balance on every admissible smooth material image.

For L>0, ρ_ℓ>0, τ_s>0, c=√(τ_s/ρ_ℓ), N≥2 and a=L/N, a stated smooth periodic wave solution and sampled chain data give a unique chain solution with ‖e‖_a≤Ca²t²/2, ‖e′‖_a≤Ca²t, max_j|e_j|≤Ca^(3/2)t²/2 and interpolation error at most max_j|e_j|+M₂a²/8, where C=c²√L M/12. Compatible nonzero-amplitude travelling modes satisfy the stated discrete dispersion iff, with error ≤c²κ⁴a²/12 when |κa|≤1.

Under countable choice and the adopted unforced constant-density incompressible periodic branch, smooth divergence-free unit-torus data have a smooth solution and unique smooth zero-mean pressure on [0,T], where T=(2C_s‖U₀‖_{H^s})⁻¹ for nonzero data and T=1 for zero data. For fixed scales, physical lifespan is T_*T; bounded smooth data have the stated common interval, uniqueness and L²-to-C(H^{s−1}) continuous dependence.

concerns.concern: Clause (iv) says 'the density is the constant reference density ρ₀' and identifies spatial velocity with ∂_tξ, while this is a branch of the exact motion model. Its consumer pthm-cm17-linear-elastic-equation-of-motion explicitly retains exact mass balance. The already proved continuity equation then forces div u=0. A nontrivial longitudinal wave has div(∂_tξ)=Aκω cos(κx₁−ωt), which is not zero. Calling the replacements first-order idealizations does not specify which exact equations are superseded. The branch needs an explicit reference-coordinate linearized balance formulation, distinguished from simultaneous satisfaction of the exact current-configuration balances. The cited [Abeyaratne text](https://web.mit.edu/abeyaratne/Volumes/RCA_Vol_II.pdf), §§11.1–11.2, printed pp. 321–322 and 328–329, formulates its linearized fields and calculations on reference regions. This affects the displacement theorem, wave-speed theorem and longitudinal-wave example.

The Statement assumes 'the model of pthm-cm17-momentum-equation: mass balance' and concludes that the exact current-region momentum equation is equivalent to a reference-variable equation after identifying material and spatial variables 'to first order.' No exact map or linearized balance interface makes that equivalence precise. For χ=X+ξ, spatial derivatives of a pulled-back field involve (I+D_Xξ)⁻¹, whereas step 1.2 uses D_X directly. The component stress-divergence calculation is correct for the separately adopted linear PDE, but the claimed exact equivalence to the earlier full continuum model is unsupported.

The example adopts the elastic branch for arbitrary A≠0 and κ≠0, without an amplitude-gradient condition. If its displacement is used in the branch's motion χ(t,X)=X+ξ(t,X), then J=1−Aκ sin(κX₁−ωt); when |Aκ|≥1 this can vanish or become negative, violating the motion prerequisite. The displayed field solves the linear displacement PDE, but it is not an admissible smooth continuum motion for all stated amplitudes. Its status as a PDE calculation versus a motion of the full branch must be made explicit, alongside the separate mass-balance issue.

The Remarks say 'the counterexample item of the companion page exhibits a motion with a vanishing Jacobian.' The companion page's sole counterexample is cex-cm17-traction-symmetry-without-stress-matrix, concerning t(n)=|n₁|n, and contains no motion or Jacobian. This is a stale reference.

The physical_scope describes 'uniform expansion of a unit cube at constant density.' The actual Example permits arbitrary L₀ and uses ρ(t,x)=ρ₀/(1+αt)³, which varies in time. The scope should distinguish constant reference density from the evolving spatial density.

Verification step 2.2 writes '0=w(2)−w(0)=2w′(0)'. The cited channel theorem permits profiles in C([0,h])∩C²((0,h)); it does not initially define a derivative at the endpoint. The immediate valid argument is that w′ is a constant on the open interval, continuity extends the resulting affine formula to the endpoints, and the two endpoint values force that constant to vanish.

alerts.finding: Statement (b) concludes 'the continuum dispersion ... is recovered with an explicit fourth-order error in the spacing.' Its displayed bound is |ω²−c²κ²|≤c²κ⁴a²/12, which is second order in spacing a for fixed κ. The fourth power is in wave number, or in κa before division by a². The batch-33 physical consumer correctly calls this a second-order spacing error.
